title: Browser app structure with ES modules
when: The user wants a small web app split into clean files, asks how to organize JavaScript, or one script has grown too long to manage.
prompt:
Goal: A no build app where each module has one job, imports are explicit, and the entry point only wires things together.
Steps:
1. Load a single entry: <script type="module" src="js/main.js"></script>; modules are deferred and strict by default.
2. Split by job: state.js (data and changes), storage.js (persistence), view.js (rendering), api.js (requests), util.js (pure helpers).
3. Named exports only; relative import paths that include the extension (./state.js).
4. No side effects at import time except in main.js, which queries the DOM, attaches listeners and calls the first render.
5. Pass dependencies in (render(root, state)) instead of sharing globals on window; events call state functions, state notifies, the view re-renders.
Quality bar:
- No circular imports.
- Pure helpers can be imported by a node:test file without a DOM.
- Files stay under about 200 lines.
Pitfalls:
- Opening index.html from file://, where module scripts are blocked; serve the folder from a local server.
- Bare specifiers (import x from "lib") that need a build step.
- Mixing default and named exports for the same thing.
Verify:
- [ ] index.html loads only main.js as a module.
- [ ] Every import path is relative and ends in .js.
- [ ] Every file parses.
- [ ] Nothing is attached to window.
Output: index.html, js/main.js and the feature modules, plus a README line on serving the folder.

examples.input: meu app.js tem 900 linhas, organiza em módulos
examples.output: main.js wiring state.js, storage.js, view.js and util.js with named exports
